Gold Butte National Monument covers nearly 300,000 acres of remote and rugged desert landscape in southeastern Nevada, where dramatically chiseled red sandstone, twisting canyons, and tree-clad mountains punctuate desolate stretches of the Mojave Desert. The brightly hued sandstone provides a stunning canvas for the area’s famously beautiful rock art, and the desert provides critical habitat. The area is popular for outdoor recreation, and visitors to the monument can hike to rock art sites, drive the Gold Butte Backcountry Byway to the area’s namesake mining ghost town, hunt desert bighorn sheep, or tour the area’s peaks and canyons on horseback. pages.title: Golf: LIV paid players millions as UK businesses owed thousands - BBC Sport
pages.description: A BBC Sport investigation has found bills to UK companies were already overdue when LIV Golf made its final payments to players and executives before filing for bankruptcy.
pages.text: Golf: LIV paid players millions as UK businesses owed thousands - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, LIV Golf filed for bankruptcy in September By Tom Grundy BBC Sport senior journalist Published 4 hours ago LIV Golf - backed by more than $5bn (£3.8bn) from Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund - paid millions to players and executives in the weeks before filing for bankruptcy, while leaving a trail of unpaid bills from UK suppliers. BBC Sport has seen invoices from five small businesses totalling hundreds of thousands of pounds, all of which were overdue before LIV made its final payments to players. Global Infusion Group, , external a Buckinghamshire company that provided catering at July's LIV Golf UK event, is still owed £321,671, due on 7 August. Suffolk-based BD365 Clean , external provided 108 cleaning staff and is owed £75,225, most of which was due on 20 July and 13 August. "It just feels completely immoral," said Bonnie May, chief executive of Global Infusion Group. "It really matters to a business of our scale. The impact has been huge, both personally and professionally." Only $2m (£1.5m) has been earmarked so far by the Saudi owners to pay unsecured creditors, leaving many smaller companies unsure if they will receive anything at all. Yet court filings reveal LIV made 59 payments to golfers on 31 July, amounting to $16.6m (£12.6m) and matching prize money for the same LIV Golf UK event. pages.description: The tech giant aims to use the near-constant sunlight available in low-Earth orbit to power data centers. The experimental satellite, launched October 1, holds four computer chips that can run Google’s Gemini A.I. for 15 minutes at a time
pages.text: Google Wants to Send Data Centers to Space—and Just Launched an Experimental Satellite to Test Whether Its Ambitious Plan Will Work Skip to main content The view from low-Earth orbit NASA On October 1, Google sent a refrigerator-size test satellite to low-Earth orbit, taking a major step in its goal of putting data centers in space. The tech giant aims to put the infrastructure to run its artificial intelligence models there so the systems can be powered by sunlight. Although far from achieving this goal, the company’s current test—part of Project Suncatcher —will assess how Google’s hardware performs in the harsh conditions of space. “This first launch is about seeing what works, identifying points of failure and applying those findings to future missions,” writes Travis Beals , Google’s senior director of paradigms of intelligence and head of Project Suncatcher, in a September 24 statement . The experimental satellite, which hitched a ride on a SpaceX rocket, was developed in partnership with the satellite imagery company Planet. It’s carrying four custom chips called tensor processing units (TPUs), which have the computing power of one server in a data center, report Kate Conger and Cade Metz for the New York Times . (The largest data centers contain more than one million servers .) The TPU chips will run for 15-minute stretches, during which they can run Google’s Gemini A.I. and process short queries. Members of the Transport Salaried Staffs Association working in areas such as rostering, service delivery and performance strategy are involved in the dispute. The union said separate votes in different areas of the business showed strong support for strikes and other industrial action but no walkouts had been scheduled yet. A GWR spokesperson said: "We continue to work with colleagues and their trades union representatives to find a mutually beneficial solution to the dispute and avoid damaging strike action." The union is calling for flexbile allowances which relate to shift work to come under basic pay, as a means of protecting salary and enhancing pension rights. It said staff who voted to strike carried out critical work that kept the railways running and services would be impacted during any walkout. Grid Cybersecurity and Communications Our nation's energy system is heavily dependent on information networks for operational reliability. Facing more dynamic behavior by electric loads at scale, the grid's operators, automated logic and--in the near future--artificial intelligence feeds on increasingly rapid timescales to manage grid assets and maintain stability. At the same time, grid-connected devices are producing and exposing more data than ever before. In fact, the next-generation power grid will be an information network as much as it is an energy network. Increasingly distributed networked grid assets present a broader attack surface for adversaries to exploit. Organized on a fixed 0.01-degree grid, approximately 1.2 square kilometers in North America, the Gridded EIF provides detailed demographic counts by age, sex, race and ethnicity as well as counts of the population by race and ethnicity and household income decile. Additionally, the Gridded EIF makes available exposure data for several key environmental hazards, including air pollution, on the same grid. By making this granular dataset accessible, we empower the research community to conduct advanced spatial analyses that yield deeper insights and surpass the capabilities of traditional aggregated place-based data studies, all while upholding the strictest confidentiality standards. pages.text: Guidance on the Protection of Personally Identifiable Information (PII) | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Guidance on the Protection of Personally Identifiable Information (PII) Personally Identifiable Information (PII) is defined as: Information that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual’s identity, either alone or when combined with other information that is linked or linkable to a specific individual. Department of Labor (DOL) contractors are reminded that safeguarding sensitive information is a critical responsibility that must be taken seriously at all times. DOL internal policy specifies the following security policies for the protection of PII and other sensitive data: It is the responsibility of the individual user to protect data to which they have access. Users must adhere to the rules of behavior defined in applicable Systems Security Plans, DOL and agency guidance. DOL contractors having access to personal information shall respect the confidentiality of such information, and refrain from any conduct that would indicate a careless or negligent attitude toward such information. Contract employees also shall avoid office gossip and should not permit any unauthorized viewing of records contained in a DOL system of records. Only individuals who have a "need to know" in their official capacity shall have access to such systems of records. pages.text: Guppy Super Guppy Oversize Cargo Transport The transportation of oversized cargo has always been a tremendous problem for logistics planners in government and private industry. The physical limitations of railroad tunnels, narrow roads, low bridges, and power lines make overland shipment of such cargo extremely problematic, if not impossible. NASA's Super Guppy offers a practical and economical solution to these problems. Although there are other aircraft capable of carrying more weight than the Super Guppy, very few come close to its internal dimensions. Boasting an immense cargo area that is 25 feet in diameter and 111 feet long, the Super Guppy can carry items that are virtually impossible to fit inside other cargo aircraft. The Super Guppy has a unique hinged nose that opens 110 degrees, permitting full frontal cargo loading. A control lock and disconnect system at the fuselage break allows the nose to be opened and closed without disrupting the flight or engine control rigging. Cargo loading is simple and efficient. There are fewer handling and shipping fixtures with a minimum of ground support equipment. A system of rails in the cargo compartment is used with either Super Guppy pallets or fixtures designed for specific cargo. Rollers mounted in the rail allow pallets or fixtures to be moved by an electric winch mounted beneath the cargo floor. Automatic hydraulic lock pins in the rail secure the pallet for flight. Guía de pruebas clínicas de dengue 26 de nov. del 2025 English (US) Puntos clave Los médicos deben considerar la posibilidad de dengue en pacientes con fiebre que vivan en áreas con riesgo de dengue o hayan viajado recientemente a estas áreas. Además de la fiebre, los síntomas comunes del dengue incluyen dolor de cabeza intenso, dolor retrorbitario, mialgia y artralgia, erupción macular o maculopapular. Para el diagnóstico de dengue agudo, los médicos deben ordenar una prueba de amplificación de ácidos nucleicos (NAAT) y una prueba de anticuerpos IgM, o una prueba de antígenos NS1 y una prueba de anticuerpos IgM. Si se sospecha dengue, los médicos deben proporcionar el manejo apropiado sin esperar los resultados de las pruebas diagnósticas. pages.description: The French film star was due to start an appeal trial after being found guilty of sexually assaulting two women on a Paris set.
pages.text: Gérard Depardieu drops appeal against sexual assault conviction Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Gérard Depardieu drops appeal against sexual assault conviction 2 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Hugh Schofield Paris correspondent Reuters Gérard Depardieu appeared at a courthouse in Paris on Monday for his appeal trial that was due to start French film star Gérard Depardieu has dropped his appeal against a conviction for sexual assault , admitting that his behaviour towards women had often been offensive and offering a "deep and sincere" apology. On the day that the appeal was due to start in a Paris court, the 77-year-old actor's unexpected mea culpa marks a dramatic reversal of his previous denials of sexual impropriety. "Justice was pronounced. I was found guilty. I understand and bow to this conviction… I have therefore decided to abandon the appeal," he wrote. It means he is now guilty in law of abusing two women during a film shoot in Paris five years ago, and his 18-month suspended prison term stands. "Victory is ours, and we welcome it with head held high," said one of the two women, named only as Amélie, who was at the court. "There is huge relief because the fight is over. The giant of film has fallen," said the other woman in the case, who is known in court by the false name Sarah. pages.description: The publisher has cancelled the US release of Shy Girl by Mia Ballard and withdrawn the UK edition after weeks of online speculation about the novel’s origins
pages.text: Hachette pulls horror novel Shy Girl after suspected AI use | Books | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Shy Girl by Mia Ballard. Photograph: PR View image in fullscreen Shy Girl by Mia Ballard. Photograph: PR Books This article is more than 7 months old Hachette pulls horror novel Shy Girl after suspected AI use This article is more than 7 months old The publisher has cancelled the US release of Shy Girl by Mia Ballard and withdrawn the UK edition after weeks of online speculation about the novel’s origins Emma Loffhagen Fri 20 Mar 2026 13.14 EDT Last modified on Fri 20 Mar 2026 14.43 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Hachette Book Group has withdrawn a horror novel after allegations circulated online that its author relied heavily on artificial intelligence. The book is to be discontinued in the UK after being published in November 2025, and its US launch date has been cancelled. The book, Shy Girl by Mia Ballard, had been scheduled for release in the US this spring under Hachette’s Orbit imprint. However, the publisher confirmed it had halted publication after an internal review. The title has also been removed from online retailers including Amazon, and will no longer be distributed in the UK. The decision was first reported by the New York Times and comes after weeks of online speculation about the novel’s origins, during which readers on platforms such as Goodreads and Reddit had questioned whether sections of the text bore hallmarks of AI-generated prose. Hemp (77') Venue: Nordic Wellness Arena Attendance: 3,879 Report (active) Scores Tables Line-ups Match Stats Head-to-head Live Text Figure caption, Highlights: Man City stay unbeaten in Champions League after win at Hacken By Michael Emons BBC Sport journalist Substitutes Lauren Hemp and Khadija Shaw scored to help Manchester City claim a vital Champions League win at Swedish side Hacken. After a goalless first half, the pair were introduced for the start of the second period in a match played in light snow on an artificial pitch. England winger Hemp scored a fortunate opener in the 55th minute when Emma Ostlund's clearance bounced off her and found the bottom corner. City pushed for a second and Mary Fowler put the ball in the net, only for it to be ruled out as Yui Hasegawa was in an offside position in front of home goalkeeper Jennifer Falk. Hemp then hit the post before playing a crucial role in City's second. Her fine pass from inside her own half released Shaw and the Jamaica striker held off a challenge and finished well past Falk to make it 2-0 after 77 minutes. Ci
